Subject: Reserved capacity ask + sensitivity to GPU prices

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the time yesterday. As discussed, HelixAI is ready to move to a reserved capacity commit to lock predictable unit economics for our production inference workloads. High-level ask: 1) a 12-month committed plan scoped to ~1,200 A100-equivalent GPU hours/month (we've attached our demand estimate), 2) a pricing structure that protects HelixAI from large month-to-month GPU spot swings, and 3) clarity on discount thresholds and approval path if we need deeper discounting.

Three specific questions for Redwood:
- Can you build a price-index clause (monthly GPU-index with a +/- band) so we both share downside risk?
- What discount tiers do you offer for commits at 1k / 1.2k / 1.5k equivalent units?
- If the market softens and we ask for a mid-term amendment, who signs off on >15% discounts?

Attaching the demand workbook and a proposed ramp plan. We're on a cadence to finalize commercial terms by the end of next week — can you confirm internal approval timelines?

Best,
Ethan

Hi Ethan — thanks for the clear brief and the attachments. High level response below and next steps.

What we can offer today (summary):
- Term & sizing: 12-month reserved commit; initial baseline 1,200 A100-equivalent hours/month with a 3-month ramp window (month 1=60%, month 2=85%, month 3=100%).
- Pricing tiers: Standard list price, then volume discounts at three thresholds: 1,000 (Tier A) / 1,200 (Tier B) / 1,500 (Tier C). Exact discount percentages are negotiable; indicative ranges: Tier A = 8-10%, Tier B = 12-15%, Tier C = 16-20%.
- GPU price indexation: we can include a monthly indexation clause tied to the Redwood GPU cost index (we'll provide the index formula). Protection band +/- 8% from baseline; outside the band we'll trigger a 30-day review with an option to adjust pass-through on a prorated basis.
- Mid-term amendments: discounts beyond 15% require Senior Commercial approval and Finance sign-off (I will route). Anything >20% needs Exec approval and legal review.

Questions for HelixAI: are you looking for a hard floor (absolute minimum price) or are you OK with shared-pass-through beyond the protection band? Also confirm whether you need a 24/7 premium SLA or standard enterprise SLA — that changes unit economics.

Next steps: I'll run this with Finance and Commercial Ops to lock an approvable range and return a marked term sheet by EOD Friday. Monica, can you help with the sensitivity model and route to Aditya for discount authority?

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
